discovery_context: Immediately after R2_12_RUNTIME_OPENED (commit 2d85a36), before any warmup or counted run, independent investigation of the real execution path required by the operative Phase B handoff was performed. That investigation inspected: (1) argine/cli.py cmd_benchmark -- the only CLI path that performs real timed inference via the real llama-server.exe process (_run_common + benchmod.run_benchmark); it exposes no --policy/--retention/--eviction/--decay argument of any kind. (2) argine/cli.py cmd_experts -- the only CLI path with an args.policy parameter; confirmed to be simulation-only (its own log line reads 'simulazione: {tokens} token, policy={args.policy}...' and it calls a pure Python analytical cost model ec.simulate(...); it never starts llama-server.exe). (3) patches/argine-experts.cpp and patches/argine-experts.h -- the compiled C++ runtime patch. Its complete environment-variable surface is exactly: ARGINE_EXPERT_STORE, ARGINE_EXPERT_DIRECT, ARGINE_EXPERT_PRETOUCH, ARGINE_EXPERT_VERBOSE, ARGINE_EXPERT_READ, ARGINE_EXPERT_BUDGET, ARGINE_EXPERT_SHARDS. None of these select an eviction algorithm. There is no evict() function, no LRU/frequency/decay logic, no enum or function-pointer for pluggable policy anywhere in the patch -- only a hit/miss/eviction counter (st.evictions) for one fixed, hardcoded cache behavior.
